title: Integer division truncates toward zero (silent precision loss)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE AVG_PCT(NUM, DEN, PCT)
C     Compute PCT = 100 * NUM / DEN as an integer percentage.
C     CLASSIC F77 TRAP: 100 * 3 / 4 evaluates left-to-right with
C     INTEGER intermediate -> (300/4) = 75. But 100 * (3/4) inside
C     the same expression style would be 100 * 0 = 0 because the
C     inner 3/4 is INTEGER division that truncates toward zero.
C     Callers expecting (NUM/DEN)*100 get 0 for any NUM < DEN.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER NUM, DEN, PCT
      PCT = NUM / DEN * 100
      RETURN
      END
notes:
Real-world bug pattern from migration projects: developers see
PCT = NUM / DEN * 100 and assume floating-point semantics. When the
rewrite uses /, the int-vs-float behaviour is ambiguous unless the
spec explicitly captures 'inputs are INTEGER, division truncates'.
The extract pipeline must flag this as an invariant AND surface the
rounding convention as an open question for the SME — silently
picking 'float division' in the rewrite is a behaviour change.
